lede: Cache 1.1 is in testing on phones and has been sent to Google Play for everyone. Work on Cache 1.2 has started; the cards below show where each part stands.

lines.text: On Google Play testing (internal, closed and open).
On TestFlight for public testers.
Google Play for everyone: sent on 23 Nov, and live once Google's review clears.
Android Auto, approved in Google's car review.
Cache 1.2.0 (55), the next test build.
Library and Bookshelves, adding PDFs with OCR, search inside your books, watched folders, and map icons for notebooks and places.

Shops, parks, landmarks and fuel shown on the map as icons you can tap; tap a town, county or area to outline it and open its summary; place cards with tap to call or open, elevation and land ownership.
Notebook entries edited on two devices at once now keep both versions. Android backups keep only your settings, never your library or device links.
Travel modes for directions (drive, walk, bicycle, dirt bike and quad or side-by-side, with on-road legs) and correct arrival times for off-road routes.
One place for API keys, with how-to steps, and road events and road work drawn on the map.

A new way for your devices to reach each other with no relay in the middle: on the same Wi-Fi with nothing to type, Nearby linking, a short link code and Cache's own QR scanner. Bluetooth, and the internet through Reticulum entry points you add, come next.

cards.title: Cache on Linux and Raspberry Pi

lines.text: The full app in a browser: maps and directions, the Library with meaning search and OCR, the PDF reader, Ask with sources, weather, chat history, models and linked folders.
A Raspberry Pi build.
A map laid out for a computer, with zoom buttons; drag to reorder stops; places highlight as you point at them.
Linking and sharing with a phone.
Notebooks, and Obsidian and Logseq folders.

cards.title: Ask: speed and accuracy
cards.goals: Goals: the first words within 15–20 s on a Pixel 8, then writing faster than you read · at least 85% of answers mostly correct

head: Pixel 8, build 54
Full answer
rows: First question after the app starts
Time to the first words of the answer

lines.text: The phone reads the question and its sources far slower than it should; most of the wait comes before the first word.
Cache keeps the work it saved between questions, so a follow-up no longer starts from scratch.
Once it starts, the answer is written faster than most people read.
Some answers skip searching your library when they shouldn't.
Fixed instructions, checked against a set of real questions before they ship.
